# Copilot Instructions — Get-R-Done Sample

Get-R-Done is a sample application built on the Continuum framework. Continuum source lives in the repository root (`../../src`, referenced via `$(ContinuumSrc)`); the repository-level `.github/copilot-instructions.md` rules also apply.

## Project Guidelines
- Do not commit or push without explicit approval; stage all changes (`git add -A`) and leave them for review.
- The system is designed with Event Modeling (screens/automations → commands → events → read models, organized into slices). The user will supply the event model; implement features slice by slice from it. The `Hello` feature

## Architecture
- Aspire orchestrates everything (`GetRDone.AppHost`): Azurite tables for Orleans clustering and the `order-documents` blob container for supporting document files, KurrentDB for event storage (no data volume until the event model exists), SQL Server with a persistent data volume for the `identitydb` database, Mailpit for local email capture, plus the Identity, Silo, and Web projects.
- `GetRDone.Identity`: Duende IdentityServer + ASP.NET Core Identity (EF Core, SQL Server) with the standard Duende Razor Pages UI (Bootstrap 5, Get-R-Done branding). `ApplicationUser` has `DisplayName` and nullable `TenantId`; `GetRDoneUserClaimsPrincipalFactory` emits `name` and `tenant_id`. Migrations live in `Data/Migrations` (use the local `dotnet-ef` tool from `dotnet-tools.json`) and are applied at startup by `IdentitySeeder`, which also seeds roles and, in Development only, demo users (`ana.ruiz@carterbank.example` with a fixed ID matching the read-model seed data, `coordinator@`, `reviewer@getrdone.local` in tenant `elliott`; `vendor@getrdone.local` with no tenant; password `Pass123$`). Emails (confirm, reset) go through `SmtpEmailSender` to Mailpit.
- Clients and AMC staff are invite-only (invitations are not built yet). Vendors self-register (`/Account/Register`) into the global vendor pool with no tenant; tenants add vendors to their fee panels later via the event model, so vendors can work for many tenants.
- `GetRDone.Silo`: Orleans silo host. Orleans Identity **server** setup belongs here (`ManagedCode.Orleans.Identity.Server`, `silo.AddOrleansIdentity()`), which requires `builder.Services.AddAuthorization()`.
- `GetRDone.Web`: Blazor Server (MudBlazor UI; `MainLayout` hosts the MudBlazor providers, app bar, and nav drawer) with cookie + OIDC auth
- Feature-based projects under `src/Features/<Feature>/`: `GetRDone.<Feature>.Abstractions` (grain interfaces, commands, responses, events) and `GetRDone.<Feature>.Grains` (implementations). No generic shared Contracts project.
- Planned: durable in-app notifications via Orleans streams + Blazor Server SignalR, with email through Mailpit.

## Multi-Tenancy
- Uses Orleans.Multitenant. Web calls grains via `ClusterClient.ForTenant(tenantId).GetGrain<T>(key)`; the tenant comes from the `tenant_id` claim.
- Event storage uses `AddMultitenantKurrentDBBasedLogConsistencyProvider` with provider name `EventLog` and connection name `kurrentdb` (see `GetRDoneStorage`). All tenants currently share the default connection.

## Projections
- Order events also target the per-user stream `clientUserOrders-{tenantId}|{userGuid}` of the user who started the order (`OrderGrain.GetStreamTargets`; names in `OrderProjections`). Targets are grain IDs; the provider maps them to the stream name the grain's own events would use.
- The Silo's `OrderProjections` KurrentDB stream provider runs a catch-up subscription on `$all` (prefix `order-`, `StartFromNow = false`) with `StreamPubSubType.ImplicitOnly`. Projection grains derive from `ProjectionGrain`, implicitly subscribe to `OrderProjections:clientUserOrders` (one grain per user), and must not override `Subscriptions`.
- Projection state uses the `Projections` memory storage with `OrleansGrainStorageSerializer`. The checkpoint store is in memory too, so both rebuild from the start after a restart.
- Stream delivery carries no user, so projection grains put `[Authorize]` on query methods, not the class, and check that the caller owns the data.
- Projection tests use `ProjectionGrainTestHarness` (Continuum.Streaming.Orleans.TestHarness): `Given` delivers events straight to the grain, and by default checks duplicate delivery and replay after reactivation. A test checks either the projected state (`Given` then `Then(state => ...)`, no `When`) or a query (`Given`, `When`, `Then<TValue>`/`ThenError`), never both. Keep one test per projection that produces on its stream, to cover the implicit subscription wiring the harness bypasses.
- Tests replace the provider with memory streams (`OrdersCluster`) and produce `StreamedEvent<object>` items directly; `GetStreamTargets` itself is not exercised by tests.


## Conventions
- Domain events are **classes, not records**. Orleans compares raised events to remove pending ones, and record value equality can match the wrong event. Events have `InitiatedBy` (string) and `OccurredAt` (DateTimeOffset), plus `[DomainEventType("GetRDone.<Feature>.<Name>")]`, `[GenerateSerializer]`, and `[Immutable]`. Events have no constructor: declare `[Id(n)] public required T Name { get; init; }` properties (IDs start at 0 per class) and create them with an object initializer.
- Aggregate state never holds events. It declares only the properties its decisions need (e.g., `OrderState.StartedBy`), and event handlers update them.
- Read models of one aggregate that must show the user's saves at once (e.g., `OrderDraft` on the order entry tabs) are `[ReadOnly]` query methods on the aggregate grain, not projections, to avoid eventual consistency. The query reads the grain's own events (`RetrieveConfirmedEvents(0, Version)`) and builds the read model from them, so the aggregate state still holds only what decisions need. The read model is an immutable record in the slice's Abstractions file that applies its own events (`OrderDraft.Start`/`Build`, and `Apply` returning a new record) and carries the stream `Version` it reflects, so the web app can apply the events a save returns without calling the grain again. Each read model call is its own slice (e.g., `OrderAggregate\Slices\GetOrderDraft.cs` with `GetOrderDraftTests`). Read models that span aggregates (e.g., `ClientOrderDrafts`) stay projections.
- Commands and responses may be records.
- `InitiatedBy` is the tenant-qualified user ID (`{tenantId}|{userGuid}`) built from the authenticated identity's GUID (`GrainUserExtensions.GetCurrentTenantUserId`), never from command input.
- IDs are tenant-qualified `TenantKeyValueObject` types created with the current tenant (`IsTenantKey`/`IsTenantGuidKey`); events store them as strings.
- Values that are only meaningful together are compound value objects in `Common.CompoundTypes.cs` (`PropertyAddress`, and the `ServiceRequestTypeRef`/`FormTypeRef`/`IntendedUseRef` Id + Version + Name references). Their `Create` combines the parts' validation and reports each invalid part under its flat name (e.g., `PropertyStreet`). Commands and events stay flat; compound types are used in validation and grain calls.
- Order entry saves one tab at a time, and each save validates that tab's required fields, so a saved tab is never incomplete (e.g., `SaveBorrowerAndAccessContact` requires `BorrowerName`). Optional values use a `CreateOptional` factory that returns `null` for empty input and validates only when a value is present; events store them as nullable strings. Optional values that go together are an optional compound (e.g., `AccessContact`): `null` when every part is empty, otherwise every part is required.
- Tab 1 (Request & Property) starts the draft with `StartOrderDraft`; after that, `SaveRequestAndProperty` changes it with the same fields and checks, except the client, which the draft keeps. In the web app, each order entry tab is a component in `Components\Client\OrderEntryTabs` that owns its fields and its save (`OrderEntryForm` shows the save's errors) and passes the updated `OrderDraft` back to the `OrderEntry` page. A save applies the `Changes` its response returns to the current draft (`OrderEntryForm.SaveDraftAsync`); only when the response `Version` shows the order moved past the draft (another browser saved it) does it read the draft again with `GetOrderDraftAsync`. Tab 4 submits with `SubmitOrderAsync` through `OrderEntryForm.SaveAsync` instead, since a submitted order is no longer a draft (`GetOrderDraftAsync` rejects it), and then goes back to Home.
- Lookups that don't belong to a real aggregate in the sample (intended uses, document types, orderable services, user directory) are pre-populated read-model grains seeded in `OnActivateAsync` when state is empty, from the injected `IReadModelSeedData` (`SampleSeedData` in the Silo). Their checks take the command's values and return a `Result`.
- Files never go through grains or events. The web app uploads a supporting document's file to blob storage first (`SupportingDocumentStore`, at `SupportingDocumentStorage.BlobPath`, never overwriting an existing blob) and then attaches the document with only its details; the event records the blob path. Only a failed `Result` deletes the upload again (best effort: wrapped in try/catch, logged, never changes the result); an exception keeps it, since the order may have attached the document. Removing a document deletes its file only after the order recorded the removal, using the blob path from `SupportingDocumentRemoved` (also best effort). The tab validates with the same value objects before uploading.
- Tests use their own data from the test project's `Data` folder (`TestData`, `RequestedByUsers`, `TestReadModelSeedData` for the `summit` tenant), never the sample's seed data. Aggregate tests use the Continuum Given/When/Then harness (e.g., `EventDrivenStateMachineGrainTestHarness`) and sign in a `RequestedByUsers` principal through `RequestContext` (`OrleansIdentityConstants.USER_CLAIMS`) before calling grains, because the test silo enforces Orleans Identity `[Authorize]`.
- Test files mirror the folders of the project they test, with namespaces to match (e.g., `OrderAggregate\Slices\StartOrderDraftTests.cs` in `GetRDone.Orders.Grains.Tests.OrderAggregate.Slices`, `ReadModels\ClientOrderDraftsTests.cs`). Shared fixtures such as `OrdersCluster` stay at the project root, and test data stays in `Data`.
- Each slice gets a `<Slice>TestData` class in the test project's `Data` folder (e.g., `StartOrderDraftTestData`), so any test's Given can reuse its events. It usually holds 3 command variations (`Command1`–`Command3`; more only when scenarios need them), each paired with a fixed user and an event factory (`DraftStarted1(orderId, occurredAt?)`). The factories build each event from its command through one mapping; `occurredAt` defaults to `TestData.At`. Compare recorded events with `Assert.Equivalent(DraftStarted1(GrainId, started.OccurredAt), started, strict: true)`. The slice's own tests run every variation through the grain, which proves the test data matches what the grain records.
- Grains return `Result`/`Result<T>`, catch and log exceptions, and never leak exception details to the UI.

## Required Setup (Known Pitfalls)
- Any project declaring `[DomainEventType]` types **and** the Silo project must reference `Continuum.Core.SourceGenerators` as an analyzer (`OutputItemType="Analyzer" ReferenceOutputAssembly="false"`). Without it in the Silo, events fail at runtime with "A type mapping for the type ... was not found."
- The Silo needs `silo.AddMemoryGrainStorageAsDefault()` so Orleans can activate event-driven grains (event state itself is stored in KurrentDB). Read-model grains use this default storage too: declare `[PersistentState("name")]` without a storage name rather than registering a named provider per grain. Projection grains are the exception (see Projections).
- Orleans version is 10.4.2 (`OrleansVersion`), required by ManagedCode.Orleans.Identity 10.4.6.
- The sample-local `Directory.Build.props` intentionally does not import the repository root packaging rules.

## Local Development
- Run `GetRDone.AppHost` (requires Docker).
- KurrentDB is pinned to port 2113 (`esdb://localhost:2113?tls=false`) so the KurrentDB desktop app can connect. It has no data volume, so data is lost when the AppHost restarts.
- Stop the AppHost before rebuilding; a running Silo locks its output files.

## Status
Hello flow confirmed end to end after pinning Microsoft.Orleans.Streaming to $(OrleansVersion), Web UI moved to MudBlazor.
- Next (infrastructure, independent of the event model):
  - Replace the placeholder `GetRDone.Identity` UI
- Next (domain): the user will create the event model; notifications are designed as part of it. After that, implement the model slice by slice.
- Optional (planned): per-tenant branding and tenant-specific URLs.
  - Branding: a tenant grain returns plain branding data (colors, logo, display name; validated value objects, no MudBlazor types); Web maps it onto a copy of `GetRDoneTheme` (the default fallback), caches per tenant, and can refresh via an Orleans stream event. Could be an event-modeled slice.
  - URLs: each tenant gets `{slug}.getrdone.com` (wildcard DNS + `*.getrdone.com` cert) and may add verified custom domains (TXT verification, per-domain managed certs). Resolve the tenant from the host via a domain registry (host -> tenant), with one canonical URL per tenant.
  - Login stays central on Identity; Web passes `acr_values=tenant:{slug}` for tenant branding on the login page, and a custom redirect URI validator accepts only the tenant's verified hosts.
  - The host is only a hint: the token's `tenant_id` must match the host's tenant; keep auth cookies host-only.
